statements.impact_statement: GHSA-53rm-773f-4q8c (RUSTSEC-2026-0523) affects the Rust crate quinn-proto from 0.11.0 to 0.11.18: one MAX_STREAM_DATA frame from a peer can open streams beyond the stream limit the endpoint advertised. quinn-proto 0.11.19 fixes it: https://github.com/quinn-rs/quinn/security/advisories/GHSA-53rm-773f-4q8c and https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0523.html . We listed the contents of every build-dev apk that the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository serves for x86_64 and aarch64 (91 versions, 2.6.4-r0 to 2.30.0-r0, with 2.6.4-r0 published for aarch64 only; 181 apks, each checked against its index checksum). Each holds one regular file, /usr/bin/build, plus its directories and no symlinks, and /usr/bin/build is a Go program in every build (it carries Go build information). No build-dev build ships uv or any other Rust program, so the quinn-proto crate is not in this package.

We listed the contents of every build-fips-dev apk that the authenticated DHI Alpine 3.23 security repository, where the FIPS packages are published, serves for x86_64 and aarch64 (91 versions, 2.6.4-r0 to 2.30.0-r0, with 2.6.4-r0 published for aarch64 only; 181 apks, each checked against its index checksum). Each holds one regular file, /usr/bin/build, plus its directories and no symlinks, and /usr/bin/build is a Go program in every build (it carries Go build information). No build-fips-dev build ships uv or any other Rust program, so the quinn-proto crate is not in this package.

GHSA-53rm-773f-4q8c (RUSTSEC-2026-0523) affects the Rust crate quinn-proto from 0.11.0 to 0.11.18: one MAX_STREAM_DATA frame from a peer can open streams beyond the stream limit the endpoint advertised. quinn-proto 0.11.19 fixes it: https://github.com/quinn-rs/quinn/security/advisories/GHSA-53rm-773f-4q8c and https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0523.html . We listed the contents of every build-fips apk that the authenticated DHI Alpine 3.23 security repository, where the FIPS packages are published, serves for x86_64 and aarch64 (91 versions, 2.6.4-r0 to 2.30.0-r0, with 2.6.4-r0 published for aarch64 only; 181 apks, each checked against its index checksum). The only Rust program in these packages is /opt/docker/dhi/uv (uv 0.13.6), which build-fips ships from 2.27.1-r1 to 2.30.0-r0. Its other programs, /usr/bin/build, /usr/bin/dhi-source and /opt/docker/dhi/yq, are Go programs. The dependency list that cargo-auditable embeds in uv names quinn-proto 0.11.18 in 2.27.1-r1 to 2.28.0-r4 and quinn-proto 0.11.19 from 2.28.0-r5, but that list can name crates that are not compiled in. reqwest uses quinn only through its optional http3 feature, and uv 0.13.6 enables reqwest without it: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/Cargo.toml . We searched the bytes of the ten distinct uv binaries (five per architecture; every shipped copy matches one of them by SHA-256) and found no quinn string at all, while the same search finds the source paths of reqwest-0.13.5 (12 times) and rustls-0.23.46 (38 times) in each. As a positive control, a stripped release build with LTO of a small aarch64 program that links quinn-proto 0.11.18 and quinn-udp 0.5.15 contains 19 quinn-proto-0.11.18 source paths, including connection/streams/state.rs, and a quinn-udp-0.5.15 path. So no build of build-fips contains quinn-proto code.

GHSA-53rm-773f-4q8c (RUSTSEC-2026-0523) affects the Rust crate quinn-proto from 0.11.0 to 0.11.18: a peer can send one MAX_STREAM_DATA frame that opens streams beyond the stream limit the endpoint advertised and exhaust its memory (a denial of service). quinn-proto 0.11.19 fixes it: https://github.com/quinn-rs/quinn/security/advisories/GHSA-53rm-773f-4q8c and https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0523.html. We downloaded every uv package the DHI Debian repository publishes for Debian 13: 44 versions, 0.11.22-0 through 0.13.10-1, for amd64 and arm64 (88 packages, each verified against the SHA-256 in the repository index). Each contains two programs, /usr/bin/uv and /usr/bin/uvx, with shell completions, manual pages, two changelogs and the copyright file; the packages up to 0.13.8-0 also carry cargo's /usr/.crates.toml and /usr/.crates2.json install records. There are no other ELF, PE or Mach-O files, no static archives and no symbolic links. The dependency list that cargo-auditable embeds, zlib-compressed, in both programs names quinn-proto in every build: 0.11.14 in 0.11.22-0, 0.11.15 in 0.11.26-0 through 0.12.15-0, 0.11.18 in 0.12.17-0 through 0.13.8-0, and 0.11.19 from 0.13.8-1 on. That list is what scanners match; it records the dependency graph cargo resolved, not the code the linker kept. In uv's lock file the only crate that depends on quinn is reqwest, whose http3 feature is the only one that enables it in reqwest 0.13.4 and 0.13.5, the versions these builds list: https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/blob/v0.13.5/Cargo.toml. None of the 93 Cargo.toml files in the uv 0.13.10 source enables http3 or names quinn, and the workspace enables reqwest with rustls and http2 but not http3: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.10/Cargo.toml. We searched the bytes of all 176 program files as unpacked from the packages, ignoring case, for the string quinn (the compressed dependency list above was left compressed, so it does not count): none contains it, so no quinn crate name, symbol or source path (such as a panic location) is present in the code, while the same search finds 12 distinct reqwest source paths and 34 to 41 distinct rustls source paths in every /usr/bin/uv. /usr/bin/uvx is a small launcher that carries neither reqwest nor rustls source paths. So no published uv build contains quinn-proto code, and the move to quinn-proto 0.11.19 in the dependency list from 0.13.8-1 changes what scanners report, not what the programs contain.
